fact: The Acting Chief Registrar says the Judiciary's Case Management System (JSDS2) has been in place since 2018.
The Judiciary says the new Electronic Case Management System (e-CMS), now fully built to replace JSDS2, has been in trial in all courts since 2 October 2023, with use to start on 1 November 2023.

The Judiciary's Chief Court Administrator named the Judiciary Electronic Case Management System (JoT e-CMS) among its platforms, and the ICT Centre director said Judiciary systems interface with 16 national institutions, enabling real-time tracking of all registered and adjudicated cases from the Court of Appeal to District Courts.
Chief Court Administrator Elisante Ole Gabriel said the judiciary's electronic case management system is gradually phasing out paper-based files, and is being expanded.
Chief Court Administrator Elisante Ole Gabriel said litigants can now file cases online from anywhere and track case progress.
The Chief Court Administrator said in February 2026 that the electronic case management system lets litigants track the progress of their cases and see which magistrate is assigned.
Deputy Registrar Richard Kabate writes in The Guardian that the Electronic Case Management System (e-CMS) was expanded across more courts during Chief Justice Masaju's first year to June 2026.

Chief Registrar Eva Nkya said on 3 March 2026 that the Judiciary's electronic case management system JOT-eCMS operates from District Courts up to the Court of Appeal and is integrated with ten stakeholder systems, six more being linked.
